direction: Eight everyday liver-care situations, large headlines and a focused app action

headline: Liver Tests
Explained
frames.scene: The same woman before work holds a liver-test handout with a friendly printed liver illustration and a simple report table.
frames.jtbd: I have liver blood-test results and want a plain-language explanation and questions to ask my doctor.
frames.visualLimit: Fictional scene. Printed liver is an illustrative handout, not a diagnostic image. No fabricated lab values or AI answer.

headline: Liver in Mind
What to Eat?
frames.scene: A man photographs his sandwich and soup at an everyday cafe.
frames.jtbd: I have liver concerns and need help making sense of my ordinary meal.
frames.visualLimit: AI-generated fictional people and an illustrative situation; not a patient testimonial or a recorded app session.

headline: Less Alcohol
Still You
frames.scene: A woman at dinner with friends declines offered wine and holds sparkling water with lime.
frames.jtbd: I want a dated record of what I drink, including days without alcohol; not necessarily a sobriety streak.
frames.visualLimit: AI-generated fictional dinner; enlarged illustrative UI detail faithfully uses existing DrinkLogView input fields. Zero is an unsaved input, not a fabricated history or recovery claim.

mockup.caption: ILLUSTRATIVE APP SCREEN
mockup.title: Log a drink
mockup.disclaimer: Alcohol tracking is for personal awareness. For alcohol-use-disorder support, consult your doctor or a certified counselor.

headline: Your Liver
Your Questions
frames.scene: A woman at home in the evening types her own question with a report on her lap.
frames.jtbd: I want to ask a question about my liver results or everyday concerns in my own words.
frames.question: What should I ask about my liver tests?
frames.visualLimit: Fictional scene and an example user question. No fabricated AI answer or clinician endorsement.

headline: Feeling Off?
Keep a Note
frames.scene: A man pauses work during a tiring afternoon and reaches for his phone to record how he feels.
frames.jtbd: I want to remember when and how I felt unwell, so I can describe it accurately later.
frames.visualLimit: Fictional everyday fatigue, not a visual diagnosis or evidence that a symptom is caused by liver disease.

headline: New Medication?
Keep the Details
frames.scene: A woman reads a plain medication carton while holding her phone to record the details.
frames.jtbd: I want to remember what I took and when, without relying on memory at my next visit.
frames.visualLimit: Unbranded fictional medication props. Recording an existing medication, not prescribing, scanning packaging, changing treatment or recommending a dose.

headline: Your Liver Story
Keep It Together
frames.scene: Hands gather dated reports and a notebook beside a phone, with a small friendly liver illustration on a handout.
frames.jtbd: I want to find my previous liver results again without searching through loose papers.
frames.visualLimit: Illustrative collection of personal papers. No invented lab values, improvement trend, recovery score or claim that this is an existing single app screen.

headline: Your Next Visit
Go Prepared
frames.scene: A man waiting for his appointment reviews his papers and prepares questions with a pen.
frames.jtbd: I want to bring my own results and questions to my next appointment and leave with fewer things forgotten.
frames.visualLimit: Fictional appointment preparation. Compact source-based Doctor Brief editor concept, not an actual exported clinical report.
